title: Soupe à l'Oignon
subtitle: French onion soup with gruyère croutons
excerpt: Onions cooked low and slow until deeply caramelised, then simmered in beef stock and finished with toasted bread and a thick crust of melted Gruyère. The great Parisian bistro soup.

recipe.sourceNotes: French onion soup has been made in France since at least the 18th century and is strongly associated with Les Halles, the great Parisian market that fed the city. The soup gratinée version, with bread and melted cheese, became the canonical bistro preparation. It was popularised in the English-speaking world largely by Julia Child, who emphasised the patience required to properly caramelise the onions, a process that takes a minimum of 40 minutes on a low heat. Quick-caramelised versions exist but produce an inferior, sweeter result.

recipeTools.notes: Wide and heavy-based for the onions.
Individual ovenproof soup bowls or ramekins are ideal for gratinéing; a heatproof serving bowl also works.

content.text: The onions need at least 45 minutes on a very low heat to caramelise properly. They should turn from white to pale gold to deep amber. They will look alarmingly like too little at first: one kilogram of onions will reduce to a fraction of their raw volume. Do not rush this stage. The sweet, complex flavour of the broth depends entirely on how dark and soft the onions are.

Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large, heavy-based pan over low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook on the lowest heat, stirring every 10 minutes, for 45 to 55 minutes until deeply golden and caramelised. Do not rush this.

Add the garlic and flour and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Season. Simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the herbs. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Heat the grill to high. Toast the bread slices on both sides. Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls. Place the toasted bread on top of each bowl and pile the grated Gruyère over the bread. Place under the hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling, and golden at the edges.
